result.stdout:
smith runs a monorepo in Node, Go, Python, Rust, .NET, Ruby, PHP, C++, Dart, the JVM, Bicep, Lua, AppleScript, VBA, Swift and Objective-C (and anything a plugin adds):
it scaffolds projects, runs their tasks in dependency order from a cache,
generates CI pipelines, and releases packages from conventional commits.

Most people start with: new (an empty folder) or adopt (a repository you
already have), then build and doctor.

Usage:
  smith [command]

Examples:
  smith                      open the interactive shell (in a terminal: ? lists the keys, : the commands)
  smith new acme             a new, empty workspace
  smith adopt --dry-run      what bringing the repository you are in under smith involves
  smith add app web --lang node
  smith build

Create:
  add                    Add a project: an app, an internal lib or a publishable package (to add a dependency, use smith install)
  adopt                  Bring an existing repository under smith: report what it involves; --init takes the steps (start here)
  architecture           Show the architecture of the workspace, or choose another
  config                 Read and change settings of smith.toml
  convert                Convert an Nx, Turborepo or mnci workspace to smith (adopt sends you here when it recognises one)
  new                    Create a monorepo: configuration, git, CI pipelines and a first commit
  remove                 Remove a project: its directory, its traces in the workspace, its CI
  upgrade                Bring the workspace up to this smith and its recipes: migrate smith.toml, regenerate the files smith owns

Work:
  build                  Run the build task (same as `smith run build`)
  deps                   Group for dependency work across projects; deps up is the same as up
  dev                    Start several projects together, such as a frontend and the API it calls
  eject                  Copy smith's default configuration of a tool into the repository, to own and edit it
  install                Add a package to a project
[truncated]
